# Overview


SaprotHub is a revolutionary platform that democratizes protein language model training, sharing, and collaboration for the entire biology community. Built around the concept of making advanced protein modeling accessible to all biologists—regardless of their coding or machine learning background—SaprotHub provides an intuitive interface for training custom protein models without requiring extensive technical expertise.

## What Makes SaprotHub Unique

### Core Innovation: Structure-Aware Protein Modeling
SaprotHub introduces **Structure-Aware (SA) sequences**, a breakthrough approach that combines amino acid residues with structural information at each position. Unlike traditional protein language models that only consider sequence data, SA sequences integrate 3D structural information encoded through Foldseek, enabling more accurate and contextually rich protein representations.

![SA Sequence Visualization](https://github.com/westlake-repl/SaProtHub/blob/main/Figure/SA_Sequence.png?raw=true)

### The Adapter Mechanism
At the heart of SaprotHub's collaborative approach is the **Adapter mechanism**, which allows researchers to train lightweight task-specific adapters while sharing a common backbone model. This approach dramatically reduces storage and communication costs, enabling efficient model sharing and collaborative development—much like grafting different fruits onto a single tree trunk.

## Architecture Overview

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "User Interface Layer"
        A[ColabSaprot] --> B[ColabSeprot]
        A --> C[ColabProtT5]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Framework"
        D[SaprotHub Platform] --> E[Adapter System]
        D --> F[Model Registry]
        D --> G[Dataset Manager]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Backbone"
        H[SaProt 35M] --> I[SaProt 650M]
        I --> J[ESM Models]
        I --> K[ProtT5 Models]
    end
    
    subgraph "Task Types"
        L[Classification] --> M[Regression]
        M --> N[Zero-shot Prediction]
        N --> O[Sequence Design]
    end
    
    A --> D
    E --> H
    F --> L
    G --> L
```

## Supported Task Categories

SaprotHub supports a comprehensive range of protein prediction tasks, organized into six main categories:

| Task Category | Description | Example Applications |
|---------------|-------------|---------------------|
| **Protein-Level Classification** | Classify entire protein sequences | Fold class prediction, localization prediction, function prediction |
| **Protein-Level Regression** | Predict numerical properties of proteins | Thermal stability, fluorescence intensity, binding affinity |
| **Protein-Protein Classification** | Predict interactions between protein pairs | PPI prediction, interaction type classification |
| **Protein-Protein Regression** | Quantify interaction strengths | Binding free energy, interaction affinity |
| **Zero-shot Mutation Effect** | Predict effects without training | Enzyme activity, virus fitness, driver mutations |
| **Protein Sequence Design** | Generate novel protein sequences | Enzyme optimization, stability enhancement, antibody design |

## Getting Started Paths

SaprotHub offers multiple entry points depending on your needs:

### 🚀 Quick Start with Colab
- **[ColabSaprot](https://colab.research.google.com/github/westlake-repl/SaprotHub/blob/main/colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb)**: Access SaProt models (35M, 650M parameters)
- **[ColabSeprot](https://colab.research.google.com/github/westlake-repl/SaprotHub/blob/main/colab/ColabSeprot.ipynb)**: Access multiple models including ESM1b, ESM2, ProtBert, ProTrek
- **[ColabProtT5](https://colab.research.google.com/github/westlake-repl/SaprotHub/blob/main/colab/ColabProtT5.ipynb)**: Access ProtT5-based models

### 🏠 Local Deployment
For users preferring local environments, SaprotHub provides comprehensive [local server deployment](https://github.com/westlake-repl/SaprotHub/blob/main/local_server) options for both Linux and Windows systems.

## The OPMC Vision

SaprotHub is the pioneering implementation of the **Open Protein Modeling Consortium (OPMC)**, a collaborative initiative aimed at:
- Fostering resource sharing and co-development
- Enabling decentralized model training
- Building a community-driven protein modeling ecosystem

The OPMC brings together multiple protein language model platforms under a unified framework, allowing researchers to contribute, share, and build upon each other's work.

## Model Ecosystem

SaprotHub supports six types of models, each serving different purposes:

| Model Type | Use Case | Description |
|------------|----------|-------------|
| **Official Pretrained SaProt (35M)** | Training | Lightweight model for rapid prototyping |
| **Official Pretrained SaProt (650M)** | Training | Full-featured model for maximum performance |
| **Self-Trained Models** | Continual training, prediction | Models you train on ColabSaprot |
| **Community Shared Models** | Continual training, prediction | Models shared on SaprotHub platform |
| **Local Models** | Continual training, prediction | Models saved locally as .zip files |
| **Multi-Model Ensembles** | Prediction | Combines multiple models for improved accuracy |

## Data Format Flexibility

SaprotHub accommodates multiple data input formats:

### Single Protein Inputs
- AA sequences
- SA sequences (structure-aware)
- UniProt IDs
- PDB/CIF structure files

### Multiple Protein Inputs
- Batch AA sequences
- Batch SA sequences
- Batch UniProt IDs
- Batch structure files

### Pair-based Inputs
For protein-protein interaction tasks:
- Pairs of AA sequences
- Pairs of SA sequences
- Pairs of UniProt IDs
- Pairs of structure files

# Quick Start



Welcome to SaprotHub - a revolutionary platform that democratizes protein language model training, sharing, and collaboration for the entire biology community. This guide will help you get started with protein modeling tasks in minutes, even without coding experience.

## What is SaprotHub?

SaprotHub is an official implementation of the [SaprotHub paper](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.05.24.595648v5) published in Nature Biotechnology. It enables biologists to train and share protein language models through a user-friendly interface, eliminating the need for advanced machine learning knowledge or coding skills.

![SaprotHub Architecture](https://github.com/westlake-repl/SaprotHub/blob/main/Figure/SA_Sequence.png?raw=true)

## Getting Started in 3 Ways

### 1. Google Colab (Recommended for Beginners)

The fastest way to start is through Google Colab, which provides free GPU access:

#### Access Options:
- **[ColabSaprot](https://colab.research.google.com/github/westlake-repl/SaprotHub/blob/main/colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb)** - Structure-aware protein models (35M, 650M)
- **[ColabSeprot](https://colab.research.google.com/github/westlake-repl/SaprotHub/blob/main/colab/ColabSeprot.ipynb)** - Sequence-based models including ESM1b, ESM2, ProtBert, ProTrek

#### Setup Steps:
1. Open the Colab notebook link
2. Switch to GPU runtime: `Runtime > Change runtime type > GPU`
3. Click the run button to start the installation (3-8 minutes)

#### GPU Selection Guide:
| GPU Type | Cost | Best For | Model Size |
|----------|------|----------|------------|
| T4 | Free | Basic tasks, small datasets | Saprot 35M |
| L4 | Colab Pro | Medium datasets | Saprot 650M |
| A100 | Colab Pro | Large datasets, complex tasks | Saprot 650M |

### 2. Local Server Deployment

For users who prefer local deployment:

#### Linux Users:
```bash
cd local_server
bash install.sh
bash run.sh
```

#### Windows Users:
1. Download [SaprotHubImage.tar](https://huggingface.co/datasets/lxzcpro/SaprotHubWindowsDeploy/tree/main) and WindowsDeploy.bat
2. Install [Docker Desktop](https://desktop.docker.com/win/main/amd64/Docker%20Desktop%20Installer.exe)
3. Run WindowsDeploy.bat
4. Start Jupyter: `bash run.sh`

#### Connection:
Connect to `http://localhost:12315/?token=SaprotHub` through Colab's "Connect to local runtime" option.

### 3. Local Installation

For advanced users who want to integrate SaprotHub into their workflows:

```bash
# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Or using Poetry
pip install poetry
poetry install
```

[pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml#L1-L34) and [requirements.txt](requirements.txt#L1-L26) contain all necessary dependencies including PyTorch, transformers, and specialized bioinformatics libraries.

## Understanding Your Tasks

SaprotHub supports various protein prediction tasks. Understanding your task type is crucial for selecting the right approach:

### Classification & Regression Tasks (Training Required)

| Task Type | Description | Examples |
|-----------|-------------|----------|
| **Protein-level Classification** | Classify entire protein sequences | Fold prediction, localization, function prediction |
| **Protein-level Regression** | Predict numerical protein properties | Thermal stability, fluorescence intensity, binding affinity |
| **Residue-level Classification** | Classify individual amino acids | Secondary structure, binding sites, active sites |
| **Pair Classification** | Predict protein-protein interactions | PPI prediction, interaction type classification |
| **Pair Regression** | Predict interaction strength | Binding energy, interaction affinity |

### Zero-shot Tasks (No Training Required)

| Task Type | Description | Examples |
|-----------|-------------|----------|
| **Mutational Effect Prediction** | Predict effects of mutations | Enzyme activity, virus fitness, driver mutations |
| **Inverse Folding** | Predict sequences from structures | Enzyme optimization, stability enhancement |

## Data Preparation

### Supported Data Formats

SaprotHub accepts multiple data types:

#### Single Protein Input:
- AA Sequences (FASTA format)
- SA Sequences (Structure-aware sequences)
- UniProt IDs
- PDB/CIF Structure files

#### Batch Input:
- Multiple AA/SA sequences (CSV format)
- Multiple UniProt IDs (CSV format)
- Multiple PDB/CIF structures (CSV + ZIP)

#### Pair Input (for interaction tasks):
- Pairs of any single input type above

### Structure-Aware (SA) Sequences

SA sequences combine residue and structural information using Foldseek encoding:

![SA Sequence Generation](https://github.com/westlake-repl/SaProtHub/blob/main/Figure/SA_Sequence.png?raw=true)

### Dataset Format Requirements

For training tasks, prepare a CSV file with three required columns:

| Column | Description | Example |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `sequence` | Protein data based on your data type | `MKTLLL...` or SA sequence |
| `label` | Task-specific labels | `0,1,2` (classification) or `1.23` (regression) |
| `stage` | Data split | `train`, `valid`, `test` |

## Model Selection

### Available Model Types

| Model Type | Use Case | Description |
|------------|----------|-------------|
| **Official SaProt 35M** | Training | Lightweight model for quick experiments |
| **Official SaProt 650M** | Training | Full-featured model for best performance |
| **Self-trained Models** | Continual training/prediction | Models you've trained on ColabSaprot |
| **SaprotHub Community Models** | Continual training/prediction | Models shared by the community |
| **Local Models** | Continual training/prediction | Models saved to your computer |
| **Multi-model Ensembles** | Prediction | Combine multiple models for better accuracy |

### Finding Community Models

1. Visit [SaprotHub Repository](https://huggingface.co/SaProtHub)
2. Browse models by task, performance, or popularity
3. Copy the Model ID for use in ColabSaprot

## Quick Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Start] --> B{Choose Access Method}
    B -->|Colab| C[Open ColabSaprot]
    B -->|Local| D[Install Dependencies]
    B -->|Server| E[Deploy Local Server]
    
    C --> F{Select Task Type}
    D --> F
    E --> F
    
    F -->|Training Required| G[Prepare Dataset]
    F -->|Zero-shot| H[Select Pretrained Model]
    
    G --> I[Choose Base Model]
    H --> J[Configure Input]
    
    I --> K[Configure Training]
    J --> L[Run Prediction]
    
    K --> M[Train Model]
    L --> N[Get Results]
    
    M --> O[Save/Share Model]
    N --> P[Analyze Results]
    
    O --> Q[End]
    P --> Q
```

## Training Configuration

For training tasks, configure these key parameters:

| Parameter | Recommended Values | Description |
|-----------|-------------------|-------------|
| `batch_size` | Adaptive (default) or 8-256 | Depends on dataset size and GPU memory |
| `max_epochs` | 10-50 | Maximum training iterations |
| `learning_rate` | 5.0e-4 (650M) or 1.0e-3 (35M) | Convergence speed control |

> [!TIP]
> Start with smaller `max_epochs` (10-20) and monitor validation performance. The best model is saved after each epoch automatically.

# Understanding Protein Prediction Tasks



Protein prediction tasks form the foundation of computational biology and drug discovery, enabling researchers to understand protein functions, interactions, and properties without expensive wet-lab experiments. SaprotHub provides a comprehensive platform for various protein prediction tasks, leveraging the power of structure-aware protein language models to deliver accurate predictions across multiple biological applications.

## Task Categories Overview

SaprotHub supports protein prediction tasks organized into seven main categories, each addressing specific biological questions and applications:

![Task Overview](https://github.com/westlake-repl/SaProtHub/blob/main/Figure/task_list.png?raw=true)

Based on the comprehensive task list defined in [task_list.md](task_list.md#L1-L144), these categories encompass the full spectrum of protein analysis needs:

## Protein-Level Classification Tasks

Protein-level classification tasks categorize entire protein sequences into predefined classes based on their properties or functions. These tasks are fundamental for understanding protein behavior and biological roles.

**Key Applications:**
- **Fold Class Prediction**: Determining the structural fold category of proteins
- **Localization Prediction**: Predicting subcellular localization (e.g., nucleus, cytoplasm, membrane)
- **Function Prediction**: Classifying proteins based on their biological functions
- **Enzyme Classification**: Assigning Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers to enzymes
- **Domain Classification**: Identifying protein domain types and architectures

**Implementation in SaprotHub:**
The platform supports protein-level classification through specialized models like the DeepLoc classifier, which can predict subcellular localization with 2-class (cytoplasmic vs non-cytoplasmic) or 10-class configurations [saprot/config/DeepLoc/cls2/saprot.yaml](saprot/config/DeepLoc/cls2/saprot.yaml#L1-L70).

## Protein-Level Regression Tasks

Regression tasks predict continuous numerical values associated with protein properties, enabling quantitative assessment of protein characteristics.

**Key Applications:**
- **Thermal Stability Prediction**: Estimating protein melting temperatures
- **Binding Affinity Prediction**: Measuring interaction strength between proteins and ligands
- **Enzymatic Activity Prediction**: Quantifying catalytic efficiency
- **Solubility Prediction**: Assessing protein solubility properties
- **Expression Level Prediction**: Estimating protein expression yields

**Technical Implementation:**
These tasks utilize regression models that output continuous values, typically trained on datasets with numerical labels representing the target property [tutorial.md](tutorial.md#L200-L210).

## Protein-Protein Interaction Tasks

These tasks analyze relationships between protein pairs, crucial for understanding cellular pathways and drug target identification.

**Classification Applications:**
- **Protein-Protein Interaction (PPI) Prediction**: Determining whether two proteins interact
- **Interaction Type Classification**: Categorizing interaction mechanisms
- **Disease-Associated Interaction Prediction**: Identifying interactions linked to diseases

**Regression Applications:**
- **Interaction Strength Prediction**: Quantifying binding affinity
- **Binding Free Energy Calculation**: Computing thermodynamic parameters
- **Interaction Kinetics Prediction**: Estimating rate constants

## Zero-Shot Mutation Effect Prediction

This advanced category uses pre-trained models to predict the effects of mutations without task-specific training, leveraging the model's learned biological knowledge.

**Applications:**
- **Pathogenicity Prediction**: Assessing disease-causing potential of mutations
- **Protein Stability Prediction**: Estimating stability changes upon mutation
- **Enzyme Activity Prediction**: Predicting functional impact of mutations
- **Immune Escape Prediction**: Identifying mutations that evade immune detection

**SaprotHub Implementation:**
The ClinVar configuration demonstrates zero-shot prediction capabilities, using the SaProt model to predict mutational effects without fine-tuning [saprot/config/ClinVar/saprot.yaml](saprot/config/ClinVar/saprot.yaml#L1-L38).

## Protein Sequence Design

This forward-looking category focuses on generating novel protein sequences with desired properties, enabling protein engineering and drug design.

**Applications:**
- **Enzyme Function Optimization**: Designing enzymes with improved catalytic properties
- **Protein Stability Enhancement**: Creating more stable protein variants
- **Antibody Design**: Engineering therapeutic antibodies
- **Vaccine Design**: Developing immunogenic protein sequences

## Residue-Level Classification Tasks

These tasks perform fine-grained analysis at the amino acid level, providing detailed insights into protein structure and function.

**Applications:**
- **Secondary Structure Prediction**: Classifying residues into helix, sheet, or coil
- **Binding Site Prediction**: Identifying ligand-binding residues
- **Active Site Prediction**: Locating catalytic residues
- **Post-Translational Modification Site Prediction**: Identifying modification sites
- **Metal Binding Site Prediction**: Finding metal-coordinating residues

## Task Architecture in SaprotHub

The platform employs a unified architecture that supports different task types through specialized model configurations:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[SaProt Base Model] --> B[Task-Specific Heads]
    B --> C[Classification Tasks]
    B --> D[Regression Tasks]
    B --> E[Zero-Shot Tasks]
    B --> F[Pair Tasks]
    
    C --> C1[Protein-Level]
    C --> C2[Residue-Level]
    C --> C3[Pair Classification]
    
    D --> D1[Protein-Level]
    D --> D2[Pair Regression]
    
    E --> E1[Mutation Effects]
    E --> E2[Inverse Folding]
    
    F --> F1[PPI Prediction]
    F --> F2[Binding Affinity]
```

## Model Selection by Task Type

Different tasks require different model architectures and training strategies:

| Task Category | Model Type | Input Format | Output Type |
|---------------|------------|--------------|-------------|
| Protein Classification | Classification Model | Single Sequence | Class Labels |
| Protein Regression | Regression Model | Single Sequence | Continuous Values |
| Residue Classification | Sequence Tagging Model | Single Sequence | Per-Residue Labels |
| PPI Prediction | Pair Classification Model | Sequence Pair | Binary/Multi-class |
| Mutation Effects | Zero-shot Model | Wild-type + Mutation | Effect Scores |
| Sequence Design | Generative Model | Structure/Constraints | Novel Sequences |

## Data Requirements and Formats

Each task type has specific data requirements:

**For Classification/Regression Tasks:**
- CSV format with `sequence`, `label`, and `stage` columns
- Sequence format varies by data type (AA sequence, SA sequence, UniProt ID, PDB structure)
- Labels depend on task type (categorical indices for classification, numerical values for regression)

**For Zero-Shot Tasks:**
- Wild-type sequence and mutation information
- No training data required
- Uses pre-trained model knowledge

**For Pair Tasks:**
- Two protein sequences or structures per sample
- Interaction labels or affinity values

> [!TIP]
> The choice between different task types depends on your biological question and available data. Start with simpler classification tasks if you're new to protein prediction, then progress to more complex regression or zero-shot tasks as you gain experience.

## Next Steps

After understanding the available protein prediction tasks, you should:

1. **[Preparing Your Dataset](4-preparing-your-dataset)**: Learn how to format your data according to task requirements
2. **[Choosing the Right Model](5-choosing-the-right-model)**: Select appropriate model architecture for your specific task
3. **[Structure-Aware Protein Representation](6-structure-aware-protein-representation)**: Understand how Saprot processes protein structure information

Each task type in SaprotHub is supported by comprehensive documentation, example datasets, and pre-configured models to help you get started quickly with your protein analysis projects.

# Preparing Your Dataset



Understanding how to properly prepare your dataset is crucial for successful protein analysis with SaprotHub. This guide will walk you through the essential steps and formats needed to structure your data effectively.

## Dataset Structure Overview

SaprotHub supports multiple dataset formats designed for different protein analysis tasks. The system is built around a flexible LMDB (Lightning Memory-Mapped Database) infrastructure that enables efficient data handling for large-scale protein datasets.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Raw Data] --> B[CSV Format]
    B --> C{Task Type}
    C -->|Classification| D[Labels: Integer Categories]
    C -->|Regression| D[Labels: Float Values]
    C -->|Token Classification| D[Labels: Per-residue Tags]
    C -->|Pair Tasks| D[Labels: Relationship Scores]
    D --> E[LMDB Conversion]
    E --> F[Ready for Training]
```

## Supported Input Formats

### CSV Dataset Structure

Your primary input should be formatted as CSV files with specific column requirements. The system automatically processes these into LMDB format for optimal performance.

**Basic Structure Requirements:**
- `sequence`: Protein amino acid sequences
- `label`: Target values for your specific task
- `stage`: Data partition (train/valid/test)

### Task-Specific Formats

#### Classification Tasks
For protein classification, your dataset should include integer labels representing different categories:

```csv
sequence,label,stage
,0,train
,1,test
```

#### Regression Tasks
For regression analysis, labels should be continuous float values representing measurements like fitness scores or binding affinities.

#### Pair-Based Tasks
For protein-protein interaction or comparative tasks, the format expands to include paired sequences:

```csv
sequence_1,sequence_2,name_1,name_2,chain_1,chain_2,label,stage
MKVLWAALLVTFLAGCQAKVEQAVETEPEPELRQQTEWD... ,MVLSEGEWQLVLHVWAKVEADVAGHGQDILIRLFKSHPETLEKFDRVKHLKTEAEMKASEDLKKHGVTVLTALGAILKKKGHHEAELKPLAQSHATKHKIPIKYLEFISEAIIHVLHSRHPGDFGADAQGAMNKALELFRKDIAAKYKELGYQG,protein1,protein2,A,B,0.85,train
```

## Data Processing Pipeline

### Automatic LMDB Conversion

SaprotHub provides automated tools to convert your CSV files into optimized LMDB format. The `construct_lmdb` function handles this transformation efficiently:

```python
from saprot.utils.construct_lmdb import construct_lmdb

# Convert your CSV to LMDB format
construct_lmdb(
    csv_file="path/to/your/dataset.csv",
    root_dir="output/directory",
    dataset_name="my_protein_dataset",
    task_type="classification"
)
```

The system automatically validates your data format and handles different task types appropriately.

### Sequence Length Management

The framework includes intelligent sequence truncation to manage computational resources:

- Training sequences: Limited to 2044 amino acids for memory efficiency
- Validation/Test sequences: Full length preserved for complete evaluation
- Token classification: Labels truncated to 1022 positions during training

## Advanced Dataset Features

### Structure-Aware Datasets

For tasks requiring structural information, SaprotHub supports specialized datasets that incorporate 3D protein coordinates:

- **SaprotLMDataset**: Combines sequence masking with structural bias features
- **SaprotFoldseekDataset**: Uses Foldseek-based structural representations
- Coordinate data is processed through the protein structure parser for optimal encoding

### Data Transformation Utilities

The framework provides comprehensive data transformation tools:

- **One-hot encoding**: For sequence representation
- **Distance maps**: Spatial relationship calculations between residues
- **Orientation features**: 3D structural information extraction
- **RBF (Radial Basis Function) encoding**: Continuous value discretization

## Best Practices for Dataset Preparation

### Quality Assurance

1. **Sequence Validation**: Ensure all amino acid sequences use standard 20 amino acid notation
2. **Label Consistency**: Verify label types match your task (integers for classification, floats for regression)
3. **Data Partitioning**: Maintain balanced train/validation/test splits
4. **Missing Data Handling**: Address gaps in sequences or labels before processing

### Performance Optimization

1. **Batch Size Consideration**: Larger datasets benefit from LMDB's memory-mapped architecture
2. **Sequence Length**: Consider truncation strategies for very long proteins
3. **Storage Planning**: LMDB files typically require 2-3x the original CSV size

### Example Dataset Files

The repository includes comprehensive examples in the `upload_files/example_csv_dataset/train/` directory:

- `[EXAMPLE]Multiple_AA_Sequences.csv`: Basic sequence classification format
- `[EXAMPLE][Classification-2Categories]Multiple_AA_Sequences.csv`: Binary classification example
- `[EXAMPLE][Regression]Multiple_AA_Sequences.csv`: Regression task format
- `[EXAMPLE]Multiple_pairs_of_AA_Sequences.csv`: Protein-pair analysis format

## Integration with Training Pipeline

Once your dataset is properly formatted and converted to LMDB, it integrates seamlessly with SaprotHub's training infrastructure. The dataset interface automatically handles:

- Data loading and batching
- Tokenization and masking for language model training
- Coordinate processing for structure-aware tasks
- Multi-GPU data distribution

## Next Steps

After preparing your dataset, you'll want to explore [Choosing the Right Model](5-choosing-the-right-model) to select the optimal SaprotHub configuration for your specific protein analysis task. The model selection process considers your dataset characteristics, task requirements, and available computational resources.

For detailed information about specific dataset format requirements and advanced processing options, refer to [Dataset Format Requirements](13-dataset-format-requirements) in the comprehensive documentation.

# Choosing the Right Model



Selecting the appropriate model is crucial for achieving optimal performance in your protein prediction tasks. SaprotHub provides a comprehensive suite of models designed for different types of protein analysis, from sequence-only predictions to structure-aware computations. This guide will help you understand the available model options and choose the one that best fits your specific requirements.

## Model Architecture Overview

SaprotHub is built around two main model families: **SaProt** (structure-aware protein models) and **ProtT5** (sequence-based protein models). Each family offers specialized implementations for different downstream tasks.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[SaprotHub Models] --> B[SaProt Family]
    A --> C[ProtT5 Family]
    
    B --> D[Classification]
    B --> E[Regression]
    B --> F[Mutation Analysis]
    B --> G[Inverse Folding]
    B --> H[Token Classification]
    
    C --> I[Classification]
    C --> J[Regression]
    C --> K[Token Classification]
    
    D --> L[SaprotClassificationModel]
    E --> M[SaprotRegressionModel]
    F --> N[SaprotFoldseekMutationModel]
    G --> O[SaProtIFModel]
    H --> P[SaprotTokenClassificationModel]
    
    I --> Q[ProtT5ClassificationModel]
    J --> R[ProtT5RegressionModel]
    K --> S[ProtT5TokenClassificationModel]
```

## Model Selection Matrix

| Task Type | SaProt Model | ProtT5 Model | Structure Required | Best For |
|-----------|-------------|--------------|-------------------|----------|
| **Protein Classification** | SaprotClassificationModel | ProtT5ClassificationModel | Optional (SaProt) | Multi-class protein labeling, functional prediction |
| **Property Regression** | SaprotRegressionModel | ProtT5RegressionModel | Optional (SaProt) | Thermostability, binding affinity prediction |
| **Mutation Effect Prediction** | SaprotFoldseekMutationModel | ❌ | Required | Zero-shot mutational scanning, variant analysis |
| **Inverse Folding** | SaProtIFModel | ❌ | Required | Sequence design from structure |
| **Token Classification** | SaprotTokenClassificationModel | ProtT5TokenClassificationModel | Optional (SaProt) | Per-residue annotation, binding site prediction |

## SaProt Models: Structure-Aware Protein Analysis

### Classification Tasks

**SaprotClassificationModel** is designed for multi-class protein classification tasks. It leverages both sequence and structural information when available, making it ideal for tasks like:

- Enzyme commission (EC) number prediction
- Gene Ontology (GO) term classification
- Subcellular localization prediction
- Protein family classification

The model supports both frozen backbone and fine-tuning modes, allowing you to choose between efficient feature extraction and full model adaptation [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_classification_model.py](saprot/model/saprot/saprot_classification_model.py#L24-L40).

### Regression Tasks

**SaprotRegressionModel** handles continuous value prediction tasks. It's particularly effective for:

- Protein thermostability prediction
- Binding affinity estimation
- Expression level prediction
- Activity measurement

The model provides comprehensive metrics including Spearman correlation, Pearson correlation, and R² score for thorough performance evaluation [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_regression_model.py](saprot/model/saprot/saprot_regression_model.py#L20-L24).

### Mutation Effect Analysis

**SaprotFoldseekMutationModel** is the flagship model for zero-shot mutational effect prediction. Key features include:

- **Foldseek Integration**: Converts 3D structures to structural sequences for efficient processing
- **Confidence-based Masking**: Automatically masks low-confidence regions based on pLDDT scores
- **MSA Support**: Incorporates multiple sequence alignment information when available
- **Comprehensive Logging**: Tracks predictions for clinical variants and research datasets

This model excels at predicting the effects of single and multiple mutations without task-specific training [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_foldseek_mutation_model.py](saprot/model/saprot/saprot_foldseek_mutation_model.py#L136-L281).

### Inverse Folding

**SaProtIFModel** specializes in protein inverse folding - designing amino acid sequences that fold into desired 3D structures. It supports:

- **Multiple Prediction Methods**: Argmax for deterministic predictions or multinomial sampling for diverse sequence generation
- **Partial Masking**: Predict only specific regions while preserving others
- **Batch Processing**: Generate multiple sequence candidates simultaneously

This model is essential for protein design applications and structure-based sequence optimization [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_if_model.py](saprot/model/saprot/saprot_if_model.py#L77-L130).

## ProtT5 Models: Sequence-Based Protein Analysis

When structural information is unavailable or when you prefer sequence-only approaches, ProtT5 models provide excellent alternatives:

### ProtT5 Classification

**ProtT5ClassificationModel** offers sequence-based classification with strong performance on tasks where structural information may be less critical. It uses the ProtT5-XL-U50 pretrained model as its foundation [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_classification_model.py](saprot/model/protT5/protT5_classification_model.py#L36-L58).

### ProtT5 Regression

**ProtT5RegressionModel** provides sequence-based regression capabilities, suitable for property prediction when only sequence data is available.

## Configuration and Usage

### Model Configuration

All models in SaprotHub follow a unified configuration system based on YAML files. The default configuration template is located at [saprot/config/default.yaml](saprot/config/default.yaml), with task-specific configurations available in subdirectories:

- **Structure-aware tasks**: Use configurations in task-specific folders (e.g., `saprot/config/DeepLoc/`)
- **Pretrained models**: Available in `saprot/config/pretrain/`

### Key Configuration Parameters

```yaml
model:
  kwargs:
    load_pretrained: True  # Load pretrained weights
    # num_labels: 2        # Number of output classes (for classification)
  
dataset:
  kwargs:
    plddt_threshold: null  # Confidence threshold for structure masking
    
Trainer:
  max_epochs: 2          # Training epochs
  precision: 16          # Mixed precision training
```

## Decision Guidelines

### Choose SaProt Models When:

1. **High-accuracy prediction is critical** and you have structural data
2. **Working with mutation effects** or variant analysis
3. **Designing proteins** with specific structural constraints
4. **Analyzing structure-function relationships**

### Choose ProtT5 Models When:

1. **Only sequence data is available**
2. **Computational resources are limited** (faster inference)
3. **Working with large-scale sequence datasets**
4. **Structure information is less relevant** to your task

### Model Selection Flowchart

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Start: What's your task?] --> B{Structural data available?}
    
    B -->|Yes| C{Task type?}
    B -->|No| H[Use ProtT5 Models]
    
    C -->|Classification| D[SaprotClassificationModel]
    C -->|Regression| E[SaprotRegressionModel]
    C -->|Mutation Analysis| F[SaprotFoldseekMutationModel]
    C -->|Protein Design| G[SaProtIFModel]
    
    H --> I{Task type?}
    I -->|Classification| J[ProtT5ClassificationModel]
    I -->|Regression| K[ProtT5RegressionModel]
    I -->|Token Classification| L[ProtT5TokenClassificationModel]
```

> [!TIP]
> When working with mutation analysis, the SaprotFoldseekMutationModel offers the most comprehensive approach, supporting both single and multiple mutations with confidence-based structural masking.

# Structure-Aware Protein Representation



SaProt introduces a revolutionary approach to protein representation by integrating three-dimensional structural information directly into the language model's embedding space. Unlike traditional protein language models that process sequences independently of their spatial context, SaProt's structure-aware representation captures the intricate relationship between amino acid sequence and protein folding, enabling more accurate predictions across diverse biological tasks.

## Core Architecture: Structure-Sequence Integration

The foundation of SaProt's structure-aware representation lies in its dual-input processing pipeline, which seamlessly combines sequence and structural information through specialized encoding mechanisms.

### Structure Encoding Pipeline

The structural encoding process begins with extracting geometric features from protein coordinates using a sophisticated feature extraction pipeline:

```python
def coords2feature(coords: dict, device: str = 'cpu'):
    pair_feature = make_rbf(coords, device=device)
    pair_feature = torch.cat([pair_feature, make_orientations(coords, device)], dim=-1)
    return pair_feature
```

This pipeline generates **407-dimensional feature vectors** that capture both distance-based and orientation-based structural relationships between amino acid pairs [saprot/data/pdb2feature.py#L19-L23](saprot/data/pdb2feature.py#L19-L23).

### Radial Basis Function (RBF) Distance Features

The distance encoding employs **Radial Basis Functions (RBFs)** to discretize continuous distance measurements into learnable representations:

```python
def make_rbf(coord_dict, num_rbf=16, device='cpu'):
    coords = torch.stack([torch.tensor(coord_dict[k]) for k in ["N", "CA", "C", "O"]], dim=1)
    coords_dist = make_dist_map(coords)
    RBFs = torch.cat([rbf(coords_dist[..., i], 2., 22., num_rbf) for i in range(coords_dist.shape[-1])], dim=-1)
    return RBFs
```

The RBF transformation maps pairwise distances between backbone atoms (N, CA, C, O) into a **16-dimensional embedding space** spanning distances from 2Å to 22Å [saprot/data/data_transform.py#L95-L115](saprot/data/data_transform.py#L95-L115). This approach preserves continuous spatial information while making it amenable to neural network processing.

### Orientation Encoding with Quaternions

SaProt captures relative orientation between amino acids through a sophisticated quaternion-based representation:

```python
def make_orientations(coord_dict, device='cuda'):
    X_N, X_CA, X_C, _ = [atom_coords for atom_coords in coord_dict.values()]
    vec_CAtoC = F.normalize(X_C - X_CA, dim=-1)
    vec_CAtoN = F.normalize(X_N - X_CA, dim=-1)
    vec_cross_product = F.normalize(torch.cross(vec_CAtoN, vec_CAtoC), dim=-1)
    
    O = torch.stack((vec_CAtoN, vec_cross_product, torch.cross(vec_CAtoN, vec_cross_product)), -2)
    dX = X_CA[..., None, :] - X_CA[..., None, :, :]
    dU = torch.matmul(O[..., None, :, :].transpose(-1, -2), dX.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
    dU = F.normalize(dU, dim=-1)
    
    rots = torch.matmul(O.unsqueeze(-3).transpose(-1, -2), O.unsqueeze(-4))
    quats = rot2quat(rots)
    O_features = torch.cat((dU, quats), dim=-1)
    return O_features
```

This process creates **local reference frames** for each amino acid using the backbone geometry (N-CA-C atoms) and computes relative orientations between all residue pairs using **quaternion representations** [saprot/data/data_transform.py#L118-L152](saprot/data/data_transform.py#L118-L152). The resulting orientation features capture both directional relationships and rotational alignments between amino acids.

## Foldseek Integration: Efficient Structure-to-Sequence Mapping

SaProt leverages **Foldseek**, a structure alignment tool, to convert complex 3D protein structures into sequences that preserve structural information:

```python
def get_struc_seq(foldseek, path, chains: list = None, process_id: int = 0, 
                  plddt_mask: bool = True, plddt_threshold: float = 70.,
                  foldseek_verbose: bool = False) -> dict:
```

This function processes PDB files through Foldseek's `structureto3didescriptor` operation, generating **structural sequences** that encode geometric relationships in a sequence-like format [saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py#L12-L38](saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py#L12-L38). The integration enables:

- **Efficient storage**: Structural information compressed into sequence format
- **Fast processing**: Leverages existing protein language model infrastructure
- **Quality filtering**: Incorporates pLDDT confidence scores from AlphaFold2 predictions

> [!TIP]
> The Foldseek integration is crucial for scalability—it converts high-dimensional structural data into a format that can be processed by existing transformer architectures without requiring specialized 3D convolution operations.

## Model Architecture: Unified Sequence-Structure Processing

### Base Model Framework

The `SaprotBaseModel` serves as the foundation for all structure-aware tasks, providing a unified interface for different downstream applications:

```python
class SaprotBaseModel(AbstractModel):
    def __init__(self, task: str, config_path: str, extra_config: dict = None,
                 load_pretrained: bool = False, freeze_backbone: bool = False,
                 gradient_checkpointing: bool = False, lora_kwargs: dict = None, **kwargs):
```

This architecture supports **multiple task types** including classification, regression, token classification, and language modeling [saprot/model/saprot/base.py#L21-L34](saprot/model/saprot/base.py#L21-L34).

### Structure-Enhanced Tokenization

SaProt employs a specialized tokenizer that processes both sequence and structural information simultaneously:

```python
def __getitem__(self, index):
    entry = json.loads(self._get(index))
    seq = entry['seq']
    tokens = self.tokenizer.tokenize(seq)[:self.max_length]
    masked_tokens, labels = self._apply_bert_mask(tokens)
    return masked_seq, labels
```

The dataset implementation supports **masked language modeling** with structure-aware tokens, enabling the model to learn joint sequence-structure representations during pre-training [saprot/dataset/saprot/saprot_foldseek_dataset.py#L59-L74](saprot/dataset/saprot/saprot_foldseek_dataset.py#L59-L74).

## Training Configuration and Optimization

### Pre-training Strategy

The pre-training configuration emphasizes structure-aware learning through carefully designed hyperparameters:

```yaml
dataset:
  dataset_py_path: saprot/saprot_foldseek_dataset
  kwargs:
    tokenizer: westlake-repl/SaProt_35M_AF2
    max_length: 1024
    mask_ratio: 0.15
```

The model uses a **15% masking ratio** for structure-aware tokens during pre-training, following established BERT-style training protocols while incorporating structural context [saprot/config/pretrain/saprot.yaml#L47-L52](saprot/config/pretrain/saprot.yaml#L47-L52).

### Learning Rate Scheduling

The training employs a sophisticated learning rate schedule with warmup and decay phases:

```yaml
lr_scheduler_kwargs:
  last_epoch: -1
  init_lr: 0
  max_lr: 4.0e-4
  final_lr: 4.0e-5
  warmup_steps: 2000
  start_decay_after_n_steps: 150000
  end_decay_after_n_steps: 1500000
```

This schedule enables **stable convergence** during the initial training phase and gradual learning rate decay to fine-tune the structure-aware representations [saprot/config/pretrain/saprot.yaml#L17-L25](saprot/config/pretrain/saprot.yaml#L17-L25).

## Feature Engineering Pipeline

### Multi-scale Structural Features

SaRot's representation captures structural information at multiple scales:

1. **Local geometry**: Backbone dihedral angles and bond lengths
2. **Pairwise relationships**: Distance and orientation between amino acid pairs
3. **Global topology**: Overall fold architecture through Foldseek encoding

### Feature Integration Strategy

The final representation combines multiple feature streams:

```python
pair_feature = make_rbf(coords, 16, device=device)
pair_feature = torch.cat([pair_feature, make_orientations(coords, device)], dim=-1)
```

This concatenation creates a **comprehensive 407-dimensional feature vector** that captures both distance-based and orientation-based structural relationships [saprot/data/pdb2feature.py#L12-L13](saprot/data/pdb2feature.py#L12-L13).

> [!TIP]
> The multi-modal feature integration enables the model to learn complementary representations—RBF features capture spatial proximity while orientation features preserve directional relationships critical for understanding protein folding patterns.

## Advantages Over Sequence-Only Models

### Enhanced Biological Realism

Structure-aware representations provide several key advantages:

- **Contextual understanding**: Amino acid function depends on structural context
- **Long-range dependencies**: Captures interactions between distant residues
- **Conformational sensitivity**: Accounts for structural changes affecting function

### Performance Benefits

The integration of structural information leads to improved performance across diverse tasks:

- **Mutation effect prediction**: Structural context crucial for understanding impacts
- **Protein-protein interactions**: Interface geometry captured in representations
- **Function prediction**: Structure correlates strongly with biological function

## Implementation Considerations

### Computational Efficiency

Despite the complexity of structural encoding, SaProt maintains computational efficiency through:

- **Pre-computed features**: Structural features calculated offline
- **Batch processing**: Optimized for GPU acceleration
- **Memory management**: Efficient tensor operations for large proteins

### Scalability

The architecture supports proteins of varying lengths through:

- **Dynamic padding**: Handles variable sequence lengths
- **Gradient checkpointing**: Reduces memory usage for large proteins
- **Distributed training**: Scales across multiple GPUs

## Next Steps

To understand how these structure-aware representations are utilized in specific applications, continue with **[Transformer-Based Model Architecture](7-transformer-based-model-architecture)** which details the transformer modifications that enable effective processing of structure-aware tokens. For practical implementation guidance, see **[Structure-Aware Sequence Generation](12-structure-aware-sequence-generation)** which covers the data processing pipeline for preparing structure-aware datasets.

# Transformer-Based Model Architecture



The SaprotHub framework implements a sophisticated transformer-based architecture that leverages both ESM (Evolutionary Scale Modeling) and ProtT5 transformer models for protein analysis. This architecture provides a unified foundation for various protein prediction tasks while supporting advanced parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques.

## Core Architecture Components

### Model Hierarchy and Base Classes

The framework is built upon a well-structured hierarchy with `AbstractModel` serving as the foundational class that extends PyTorch Lightning [saprot/model/abstract_model.py](saprot/model/abstract_model.py#L12-L405). This abstract base defines the essential interface for all models, including methods for model initialization, forward propagation, metric handling, and checkpoint management. Two primary concrete implementations extend this foundation:

- **SaprotBaseModel**: Utilizes ESM transformer architecture for structure-aware protein representation
- **ProtT5BaseModel**: Implements ProtT5 transformer for sequence-based protein analysis

Both base models share common patterns but differ in their underlying transformer architectures and tokenization strategies.

### ESM-Based Architecture (Saprot)

The SaprotBaseModel implements ESM-based transformers with sophisticated structure integration capabilities [saprot/model/saprot/base.py](saprot/model/saprot/base.py#L21-L453):

```python
class SaprotBaseModel(AbstractModel):
    """
    ESM base model. It cannot be used directly but provides model initialization for downstream tasks.
    """
```

The model initialization process dynamically selects appropriate transformer architectures based on task requirements:

- **Classification Tasks**: Utilizes `AutoModelForSequenceClassification` for multi-class protein predictions
- **Token Classification**: Implements sequence-level labeling capabilities
- **Regression Tasks**: Supports continuous value prediction

The ESM architecture excels at capturing both sequence and structural information through its attention mechanisms, making it particularly suitable for structure-aware protein analysis.

### ProtT5-Based Architecture

The ProtT5BaseModel leverages the T5 encoder-decoder architecture adapted specifically for protein sequences [saprot/model/protT5/base.py](saprot/model/protT5/base.py#L27-L393):

```python
class ProtT5BaseModel(AbstractModel):
    """
    T5 base model. It cannot be used directly but provides model initialization for downstream tasks.
    """
```

ProtT5 uses the `T5Tokenizer` and `T5EncoderModel` components, providing robust sequence understanding capabilities. The architecture is particularly effective for tasks requiring deep sequence comprehension and can be extended with custom classification heads for specific protein prediction tasks.

## Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning with LoRA

Both architectures implement advanced Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) techniques for efficient fine-tuning, enabling parameter-efficient adaptation to specific tasks while preserving the knowledge captured in pre-trained weights.

### LoRA Configuration and Management

The framework supports sophisticated LoRA configurations with multiple adapter management [saprot/model/saprot/base.py](saprot/model/saprot/base.py#L74-L120):

```python
lora_config = {
    "task_type": "SEQ_CLS",
    "target_modules": ["query", "key", "value", "intermediate.dense", "output.dense"],
    "modules_to_save": ["classifier"],
    "inference_mode": False,
    "r": getattr(self.lora_kwargs, "r", 8),
    "lora_dropout": getattr(self.lora_kwargs, "lora_dropout", 0.0),
    "lora_alpha": getattr(self.lora_kwargs, "lora_alpha", 16),
}
```

For ProtT5 models, the target modules are specifically tailored to the T5 architecture [saprot/model/protT5/base.py](saprot/model/protT5/base.py#L79-L125):

```python
"target_modules": ["SelfAttention.q", "SelfAttention.k", "SelfAttention.v", "SelfAttention.o", 
                   "EncDecAttention.q", "EncDecAttention.k", "EncDecAttention.v", "EncDecAttention.o"]
```

### Multi-Adapter Support

The framework supports loading and managing multiple LoRA adapters simultaneously, enabling:

- **Transfer Learning**: Loading pre-trained adapters for specific domains
- **Multi-Task Learning**: Maintaining separate adapters for different tasks
- **Adapter Composition**: Combining multiple adapters for enhanced performance

## Hidden State Extraction and Representation

Both architectures provide sophisticated methods for extracting and processing transformer hidden states, enabling flexible feature extraction for various downstream applications.

### Hidden State Processing

The `get_hidden_states_from_dict` method demonstrates the sophisticated approach to representation learning [saprot/model/saprot/base.py](saprot/model/saprot/base.py#L257-L290):

```python
def get_hidden_states_from_dict(self, inputs: dict, reduction: str = None) -> list:
    """
    Get hidden representations from input dict
    
    Args:
        inputs: A dictionary of inputs containing ["input_ids", "attention_mask", "token_type_ids"]
        reduction: Whether to reduce the hidden states ("mean" for averaging over sequence length)
    
    Returns:
        hidden_states: List of tensors with shape [L, D] where L is sequence length and D is hidden dimension
    """
```

This method intelligently handles EOS token detection and provides flexible reduction strategies for different use cases, supporting both token-level and sequence-level representations.

## Structure Integration Capabilities

A key innovation in the Saprot architecture is the seamless integration of structural information into transformer representations through bias features.

### Structure-Aware Attention

The `add_bias_feature` method enables structure integration by adding coordinate-derived features to attention mechanisms [saprot/model/saprot/base.py](saprot/model/saprot/base.py#L327-L336):

```python
def add_bias_feature(self, inputs, coords: List[Dict]) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Add structure information as biases to attention map. This function is used to add structure information
    to the model as Evoformer does.
    
    Args:
        inputs: Input dictionary with ["input_ids", "attention_mask", "token_type_ids"]
        coords: Coordinates of backbone atoms with keys ["N", "CA", "C", "O"]
    
    Returns:
        pair_feature: Tensor of shape [B, L, L, 407] representing RBF of distance(400) + angle(7)
    """
```

This approach enables the transformer to incorporate 3D structural information directly into its attention mechanisms, significantly enhancing the model's ability to understand protein structure-function relationships.

## Task-Specific Implementations

The framework provides specialized implementations for various protein prediction tasks, each tailored to leverage the transformer architecture effectively.

### Classification Models

Classification implementations demonstrate the practical application of the transformer architecture [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_classification_model.py](saprot/model/saprot/saprot_classification_model.py#L10-L82):

```python
class SaprotClassificationModel(SaprotBaseModel):
    def forward(self, inputs, coords=None):
        if coords is not None:
            inputs = self.add_bias_feature(inputs, coords)
        
        if self.freeze_backbone:
            # Extract and process hidden states for frozen backbone
            repr = torch.stack(self.get_hidden_states_from_dict(inputs, reduction="mean"))
            x = self.model.classifier.dropout(repr)
            x = self.model.classifier.dense(x)
            x = torch.tanh(x)
            x = self.model.classifier.dropout(x)
            logits = self.model.classifier.out_proj(x)
        else:
            logits = self.model(**inputs).logits
        
        return logits
```

The ProtT5 classification model follows similar patterns but is adapted to the T5 architecture [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_classification_model.py](saprot/model/protT5/protT5_classification_model.py#L10-L106):

```python
class ProtT5ClassificationModel(ProtT5BaseModel):
    def forward(self, inputs, coords=None):
        if coords is not None:
            inputs = self.add_bias_feature(inputs, coords)
        
        if self.freeze_backbone:
            # Similar processing for frozen backbone
            repr = torch.stack(self.get_hidden_states_from_dict(inputs, reduction="mean"))
            # ... classifier processing
        else:
            outputs = self.model(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask)
            repr = outputs.last_hidden_state[:, 1: -1].mean(dim=1)
            logits = self.model.classifier(repr)
        
        return logits
```

## Architecture Comparison

| Feature | ESM-Based (Saprot) | ProtT5-Based |
|---------|-------------------|--------------|
| **Base Architecture** | ESM Transformer | T5 Encoder |
| **Tokenizer** | AutoTokenizer | T5Tokenizer |
| **LoRA Target Modules** | query, key, value, intermediate.dense, output.dense | SelfAttention.*, EncDecAttention.* |
| **Structure Integration** | Native support via bias features | Supported via bias features |
| **Hidden State Access** | outputs["hidden_states"][-1] | outputs.last_hidden_state |
| **Best For** | Structure-aware tasks, complex protein representations | Sequence analysis, transfer learning |
